title: Normalized compact-support composition satisfies the projection mate identity
statement:
Let $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$ have characteristic $p$, fix a prime $\ell\ne p$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ with valuation ring $\mathcal O_E$ and uniformizer $\varpi_E$, and put $A_{E,n}=\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^n$ for $n\ge1$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Let $X\xrightarrow fY\xrightarrow gZ$ be separated finite-type morphisms of finite-type $k$-schemes. At a finite coefficient ring $\Lambda=A_{E,n}$ choose a compactification $Y\xhookrightarrow{i}\overline Y\xrightarrow{s}Z$ of $g$, and choose a compatible compactification triangle for $f$ consisting of an open immersion $j:X\hookrightarrow V$, an open immersion $b:V\hookrightarrow\overline X$, a proper map $q:V\to Y$, and a proper map $p:\overline X\to\overline Y$ such that $f=qj$ and $pb=iq$; the composite $bj$ compactifies $gf$ and the compact-support composition comparison is the canonical mate
$$\alpha_{g,f}:Rg_!Rf_!\xrightarrow{\sim}R(gf)_!$$
obtained from this triangle and the normalized proper/open comparison. For arbitrary ambient derived inputs $K$ on $X$ and $L$ on $Z$, let $\operatorname{PF}$ be the counit-defined projection transformations of [def-exchange-projection]. Then the normalized mate calculation gives
$$\alpha_{g,f,K\otimes^LLf^*Lg^*L}\,Rg_!(\operatorname{PF}_{f,K,Lg^*L})\,\operatorname{PF}_{g,Rf_!K,L}
=\operatorname{PF}_{gf,K,L}(\alpha_{g,f,K}\otimes1).$$
The equality is between the specified composites after inserting the canonical pullback, tensor, and direct-image associators; it is natural in $K,L$, needs no Tor or constructibility hypotheses, and is compatible with the associative compositor for three composable morphisms. The same displayed identity holds in $D(\mathscr S_Z)$ for arbitrary strict semilinear system inputs $K,L$, before finite evaluation or total limit. Here $\mathscr S_T$ is the category of systems of $(A_{E,n})_T$-module sheaves, and the operations, counit-defined projections and normalized proper/open system maps are the simultaneous ringed-diagram-site constructions of [lem-sf-integral-compactification-system-realization]; $R h_!$ means $S_pJ_j$ for the indicated compactification. The intermediate system maps are the specified ones, with their quotient transitions. Neither separatedness of $X,Y,Z$ over $k$ nor faithfulness of evaluation on derived maps is assumed.

proof.text: All schemes in the supplied triangle are finite type over $k$. A field is Noetherian since its only ideals are $0,k$, so the finite-type lemma makes these schemes Noetherian. Each inverse image of an affine open under $j,b,i$ is an open subscheme of the Noetherian source of that map, hence quasi-compact by the open-subscheme lemma. Thus these opens, and $bj$, are quasi-compact, as required below. Work first on the finite-coefficient unbounded pro-etale categories. Write $P_h=Lh^*$, $S_h=Rh_*$ and $J_e=e_!$, and write $\pi_h$ and $\delta_e$ for the proper counit projection and open tensor maps. Use the triangle already supplied in the statement; do not replace it by a Cartesian triangle. Put $F=S_qJ_j$, $G=S_sJ_i$, $H=S_{sp}J_{bj}$ and $\gamma=\Gamma_{(b,i,q,p)}$. If $C:S_sS_pJ_bJ_j\cong H$ is the composite of $c_{s,p}$ and $e_{b,j}$ of the ambient pasting lemma, the specified normalization is exactly $\alpha=C\circ S_s(\gamma J_j)$. This is the definition of the comparison in the question, rather than a transport from an etale-origin composition theorem. The projection definition reads $\operatorname{PF}_f=S_q(\delta_j)\pi_q$, $\operatorname{PF}_g=S_s(\delta_i)\pi_s$ and $\operatorname{PF}_{gf}=S_{sp}(\delta_{bj})\pi_{sp}$, with the indicated pullbacks in each $\delta$.

proof.text: For composable maps $u,v$, identify $P_{vu}=P_uP_v$ and $S_{vu}=S_vS_u$ by the conjugate compositors of the ambient lemma. The composite adjunction has counit $\varepsilon_u\circ P_u\varepsilon_vS_u$. The transpose of $S_v(\pi_{u;M,P_vN})\pi_{v;S_uM,N}$ is therefore $(\varepsilon_{u,M}\otimes1)\circ(P_u\varepsilon_{v,S_uM}\otimes1)\circ\mu_{P_uP_v}$: substitute the counit-transpose formula twice and use naturality of $\mu_u$ and the adjunction triangle identity. This is precisely the transpose defining $\pi_{vu}$ for that composite counit. Injectivity of the adjunction bijection gives, restoring $c$, $$\pi_{vu}(c_{v,u,M}\otimes1)=c_{v,u,M\otimes P_uP_vN}\,S_v(\pi_u)\,\pi_v.$$ This is a calculation of maps; no projection is inverted.

proof.text: For opens $j,b$ and $M,N$ on their source and target, respectively, $$\delta_{bj}(e_{b,j,M}\otimes1)=e_{b,j,M\otimes P_jP_bN}\,J_b(\delta_j)\,\delta_b.$$ Indeed, the tensor source is isomorphic, by $\delta_b$ and $J_b\delta_j$, to an object in the image of $J_bJ_j\cong J_{bj}$. Both arrows become the identity on $M\otimes P_jP_bN$ after $P_{bj}$, by the open-unit normalization. Full faithfulness of $J_{bj}$ proves their equality. This uses restriction to the open, where it is fully faithful, rather than evaluation of a coefficient system.

proof.text: Put $T=P_sL$, $U=P_iT=P_gL$, $M=J_jK$ and $K'=K\otimes P_jP_qU=K\otimes P_fP_gL$. Apply the finite-coefficient clause of the proper/open projection-mate lemma to the actual commutative square $pb=iq$, with inputs $M,T$. It gives $$\gamma_{M\otimes P_qU}\,J_i(\pi_{q;M,U})\,\delta_i=S_p(\delta_b)\,\pi_{p;J_bM,T}\,(\gamma_M\otimes1).$$ The proper maps are exactly $q,p$ and the open maps are $b,i$; a Cartesian square is not required. Naturality of $\gamma$ with respect to $\delta_j:M\otimes P_qU\to J_jK'$ replaces $\gamma_{J_jK'}J_iS_q(\delta_j)$ by $S_pJ_b(\delta_j)\gamma_{M\otimes P_qU}$. The resulting map is $$C_{K'}\,S_sS_p\bigl(J_b(\delta_j)\circ\delta_b\bigr)\,S_s(\pi_p)\,\pi_s\,(S_s\gamma_M\otimes1).$$ The source is $GF K\otimes L$ and the target is $HK'$. Apply step 3 with opens $j,b$ and tensor factor $P_{sp}L$ to replace $J_b(\delta_j)\delta_b$ under $e_{b,j}$ by $\delta_{bj}$. Naturality of the two compositors then makes the expression in step 5 equal to $$S_{sp}(\delta_{bj})\pi_{sp}(C_K\otimes1)(S_s\gamma_M\otimes1)=\operatorname{PF}_{gf}(\alpha_K\otimes1).$$ This proves the displayed finite-coefficient identity. proof.text: Now work intrinsically in $D(\mathscr S_T)$, with $P,S,J$, tensor, units and counits from the simultaneous system models. The ambient pasting lemma supplies conjugate compositors on these unbounded system categories, so the transpose calculation of step 2 and the fully faithful open restriction calculation of step 3 apply to system maps. Crucially use the SYSTEM clause of the proper/open projection-mate lemma with $M=J_jK$, $T=P_sL$. It gives in $D(\mathscr S_{\overline Y})$ exactly $$\gamma_{M\otimes P_qP_iT}J_i(\pi_q)\delta_i=S_p(\delta_b)\pi_p(\gamma_M\otimes1).$$ Whisker this system equality by $S_s$ and postcompose by $C_{K'}S_sS_pJ_b(\delta_j)$. Naturality of the system $\gamma$ and $\pi_s$ gives the expression displayed in step 5. The two system identities from steps 2 and 3 turn that expression into the right-hand side displayed in step 6. All factors, including quotient transitions, belong to the same ringed diagram models; no evaluated equality or total-limit argument is used.

proof.text: For later comparison of compactifications, take a proper refinement $u:c_1\to c_2$, $c_a=(j_a,p_a)$, so $uj_1=j_2$ and $p_2u=p_1$. Let $C_u:S_{p_2}J_{j_2}\to S_{p_1}J_{j_1}$ be $S_{p_2}\Gamma_{(j_1,j_2,1,u)}$ followed by the direct-image compositor. Apply the proper/open mate identity with $r=1$, input $K$, and tensor factor $P_{p_2}L$. The defining transpose for $\pi_1$ is the identity. Thus it reads $$\Gamma_{K\otimes P_{j_2}P_{p_2}L}\delta_{j_2}=S_u(\delta_{j_1})\pi_u(\Gamma_K\otimes1).$$ Apply $S_{p_2}$ and precompose by $\pi_{p_2}$; step 2 with $u,p_2$ gives $$C_u(K\otimes P_fL)\operatorname{PF}^{c_2}=\operatorname{PF}^{c_1}(C_uK\otimes1).$$ This proves the required refinement compatibility for arbitrary inputs, in both coefficient settings, without the bounded constructible/finite-Tor refinement lemma. It is an equation in the direction of the specified refinement maps and uses no inverse of $C_u$.

proof.text: An arbitrary supplied triangle can first be refined to a Cartesian one. Its induced $V\to\overline X\times_{\overline Y}Y$ is clopen by the ambient lemma. Let $W\hookrightarrow\overline X$ be the schematic closure of $X$ supplied by the closure lemma; its hypotheses hold because $\overline X$ is finite type over the Noetherian field $k$, hence Noetherian and quasi-separated. The open $W_Y=W\times_{\overline Y}Y$ has dense open $X$ and its complementary clopen piece outside $V$ misses $X$, so that piece is empty. Thus $W_Y\to\overline X_Y$ factors through the open $V$ and is a closed immersion there (restriction of the closed immersion $W\hookrightarrow\overline X$). The maps $W\to\overline X$ and $W_Y\to V$ are proper, and $W\to\overline Y$ is proper by composition. The induced open $X\to W_Y$ and $W_Y\to W$, with proper $W_Y\to Y$, therefore form a Cartesian refining triangle. All arrows restrict to the identity on $X$ and satisfy the original triangle equations. These are geometric operations; the refinement projection identity is already proved in step 8 on both coefficient domains.

proof.text: First use step 9 for every supplied non-Cartesian triangle. For three composable maps, arrange compatible compactifications in one refining tower: apply the compatible-tower construction successively to the two adjacent pairs, then its common-refinement clause to compare two choices. The cofiltered compactification lemma permits incorporating any previously supplied compactifications; repeat for the finite list of ambient and intermediate schemes. In the resulting grid let $A,B,C$ denote the three proper/open cells of Stacks Tag 0F7K (lemma-pseudo-functor). As in 0F7K, one composition path uses $\gamma_C$ followed by $\gamma_{A+B}$ and the other uses $\gamma_A$ followed by $\gamma_{B+C}$, with their functor whiskerings. Vertical and horizontal pasting from the ambient lemma replace the rectangle maps by their constituent $\Gamma_A,\Gamma_B,\Gamma_C$. The transformations for $A$ and $C$ act in disjoint functor positions, so their two whiskering orders agree by naturality. The unital associative $c,e$ finish the equality on the common tower. Pasting applied to the squares between refining towers gives the same equation with the directed refinement maps inserted, so the construction is compatible with either original parenthesization and its specified comparison maps. This argument concerns the actual unbounded pro-etale or system transformations, not the bounded-below etale-origin compositor.

Both identify the threefold iterated projection map with $\operatorname{PF}_{hgf}$ after the corresponding composition path. Step 10 equates those paths on the common tower, and step 8 intertwines every projection map with each directed refinement comparison to that tower. Consequently these projection identities commute with the associative compositor and with the comparisons between the two compactifications of $hgf$.
